title: China, Not Iran, Is Trump’s Real Foreign-Policy Debacle
gist: Nicholas Bequelin and Yaqiu Wang argue that, ahead of Xi Jinping's Sept. 24 Washington summit, Trump's incoherent China policy has let Beijing gain ground on trade leverage, rare-earth chokepoints, AI, military deterrence around Taiwan and soft power in just 19 months, a more consequential failure than the Iran war. The damage is self-inflicted and long-term, confirming Xi's belief that time is on China's side.

insights.claim: According to a Peterson Institute study, the U.S.-China trade war did not really shrink the deficit but rerouted Chinese exports through third countries, chiefly Vietnam, Taiwan and Mexico.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Transshipment hubs (Vietnam, Mexico, Taiwan) are beneficiaries of tariff rerouting and also targets for future U.S. rules-of-origin crackdowns.
insights.locator: Exhibit one is the trade deficit

insights.claim: Weighed against the costs of tariff volatility on U.S. manufacturers and consumers, the authors judge Trump's tariff policy a net negative for the U.S. economy.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Tariff uncertainty is framed as a persistent drag on U.S. industrial margins rather than a reshoring tailwind.
insights.locator: Exhibit one is the trade deficit

insights.claim: The administration failed to reduce U.S. supply-chain dependence on China for rare earths, magnets and broad swaths of industrial inputs, and did not anticipate that Beijing would use those chokepoints against punitive tariffs.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Rare-earth and magnet dependence remains China's most potent retaliation lever; non-China rare-earth supply chains stay strategically valuable.
insights.locator: Second, and more critically

insights.claim: U.S. farm revenues are largely hostage to Chinese purchases of soybeans and animal products, which forced Trump into a truce when Beijing retaliated against tariff threats.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Chinese ag purchases are a tell for the state of the truce; soybean export data is a practical monitor of U.S.-China tensions.
insights.locator: Second, and more critically

insights.claim: At the October 2025 Busan meeting on the sidelines of APEC, Trump dropped his threat of an additional 100 percent tariff on Chinese imports in exchange for a fragile truce on rare earths, soybeans, fentanyl and export controls.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Shows the practical ceiling on U.S. tariff escalation against China; markets should discount maximalist tariff threats.
insights.quote: The rest of the world duly took note of the limits of American economic leverage with China.
insights.locator: The bigger implications for U.S. economic security

insights.claim: Like Iran's discovery via the Strait of Hormuz blockade, China has shown it can withstand, work around and retaliate against even Washington's most aggressive trade-war measures.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Adversaries now understand the limits of U.S. coercion, which raises odds of retaliation rather than capitulation in future standoffs.
insights.locator: The bigger implications for U.S. economic security

insights.claim: China's large language models now rival and in some functions exceed U.S. models at a fraction of the cost, and its open-weight models, manufacturing strength and lead in industrial robot deployment help it spread AI at home and abroad.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Cost-competitive Chinese open models pressure pricing power of U.S. AI labs, especially in global-south and industrial adoption markets.
insights.locator: Most damaging in the long term

insights.claim: China is making steady progress on its key AI weakness, limited computing power.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Watch Chinese domestic chip capacity; closing the compute gap would erode the moat of U.S. semiconductor export controls.
insights.locator: Most damaging in the long term

insights.claim: The Trump administration failed to sustain Biden-era advanced semiconductor controls and moved too slowly against workarounds, letting Chinese firms train models on banned chips obtained directly or via third countries.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Chip export policy is reactive and leaky; expect episodic blacklistings rather than a coherent regime, adding headline risk for chip names.
insights.quote: Export controls can buy time, but their effectiveness depends on anticipating how a rival will adapt.
insights.locator: Trump keeps claiming that the United States

insights.claim: National power depends less on pure innovation than on dominating the full cycle of a general-purpose technology: discovery, commercialization and diffusion at scale, a measure on which the U.S. looks far weaker.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Record U.S. markets and capitalization may overstate strategic advantage; diffusion and deployment metrics matter more.
insights.locator: Some observers will object

insights.claim: China is on track to produce nearly twice as many STEM Ph.D.s per year as the U.S., files more patents while closing the gap on high-quality ones, and recruits talent that punitive U.S. immigration rules turn away.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Talent-pipeline divergence is a slow-moving but durable input to long-run tech competitiveness.
insights.locator: While Washington attacks universities

insights.claim: While the White House dismantles support for wind, EVs and clean energy, China is consolidating global dominance in batteries, solar and EVs and running record trade surpluses increasingly powered by high-tech exports.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Clean-tech manufacturing leadership continues to consolidate in China; U.S. clean-energy names face policy headwinds.
insights.locator: While Washington attacks universities

insights.claim: The Iran war diverted U.S. forces from Asia: redeploying the USS George Washington from Japan to the Middle East left the Western Pacific without a U.S. carrier.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: A thinner U.S. presence in the Western Pacific raises Taiwan Strait tail risk during the Iran conflict.
insights.locator: On each count, deterrence has weakened

insights.claim: The Iran conflict has consumed large quantities of long-range precision missiles, Patriot and THAAD interceptors and Tomahawks that would be critical in a conflict with China.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Munitions depletion supports a multi-year replenishment cycle for missile and interceptor makers.
insights.locator: On each count, deterrence has weakened

insights.claim: Since late 2025 Beijing has run its largest and closest exercises around Taiwan, rehearsed blockades, simulated strikes on U.S.-supplied systems and surveyed Taiwan's eastern EEZ, while Trump treated a $14 billion Taiwan arms package as a negotiating chip.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Signals that Taiwan's security is tradeable in U.S.-China bargaining, a key variable for Taiwan-exposed assets ahead of the Xi summit.
insights.quote: Trump’s treatment of a $14 billion arms package as a “negotiating chip” has signaled to Beijing
insights.locator: Messaging has fared no better

insights.claim: Weakened U.S. security assurances are pushing Asian states to hedge: Trump ordered a substantial cut to the U.S.-South Korea military exercise and President Lee Jae-myung is seeking full restoration of relations with China.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Korea-China rapprochement could benefit Korean exporters to China while loosening alliance cohesion.
insights.locator: Across the region, the weakening

insights.claim: Washington has needlessly strained ties with India, and Beijing and New Delhi, while distrustful, are pragmatically converging through BRICS around alternative trade and financial systems insulated from U.S. interference.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Growth of non-dollar trade and payment rails via BRICS is a slow-moving de-dollarization risk worth tracking.
insights.locator: Across the region, the weakening

insights.claim: In a Pew Research Center 2026 survey of 36 countries, only 39 percent said the U.S. government respects its people's personal freedoms and 56 percent said it does not, and Pew now finds China viewed more favorably than the U.S. in 25 places.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Declining U.S. favorability weakens its ability to rally coalitions for sanctions or tech controls.
insights.locator: At home, Trump’s aggressive immigration crackdown

insights.claim: Brand Finance's 2026 Global Soft Power Index recorded the largest decline for the U.S. among all 193 countries assessed.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Reputational erosion can feed into tourism, education exports and brand-driven U.S. consumer exports abroad.
insights.locator: Trump’s MAGA political culture

insights.claim: U.S. foreign aid fell 57 percent in 2025 after the dismantling of USAID, leaving the U.S. providing less international aid than Germany.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Aid retreat opens space for Chinese development finance and influence in emerging markets.
insights.locator: Foreign aid was once another important source

insights.claim: After capturing Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in January, Washington struck an oil arrangement giving the U.S. government a 35 percent stake in a company controlling major Venezuelan oil fields.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: U.S. state equity in Venezuelan oil is a novel resource-nationalism model with implications for Venezuelan supply and energy majors.
insights.locator: Trump has also increasingly relied on military coercion

insights.claim: Cuts to democracy programs, the National Endowment for Democracy and Radio Free Asia have reduced scrutiny of Beijing's repression and given China more room to reshape international norms and the U.N. human rights system.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Weaker norm constraints make it easier for authoritarian states to pursue foreign-policy goals, raising structural governance risk in EM.
insights.locator: There is a more direct international dimension

themes.theme: Why the China failure is underrated

insights.claim: The China policy failure is under-recognized because the administration never set a stable hierarchy of China objectives and its 2025 National Security Strategy framed China mainly as an economic, not paramount geopolitical, challenge.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Absence of clear China goals implies continued policy volatility and transactional swings around summits.
insights.locator: If China has not yet been recognized

insights.claim: China is not trying to build a Chinese world order but to constrain U.S. power, push the U.S. out of Asia, blunt its financial leverage, weaken Western institutions and discredit its democracy.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Reframes Chinese strategy as spoiling rather than replacing, targeting U.S. financial leverage such as sanctions and dollar dominance.
insights.locator: China, contrary to much commentary

insights.claim: Despite China struggling with a property-debt hangover, adverse demographics and stalled reforms, and squandering chances as its export machine provokes backlash, Beijing does not need global embrace to benefit from U.S. retreat.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Relative, not absolute, strength is what matters; bearish China macro data does not negate strategic gains.
insights.quote: Perhaps Trump’s greatest legacy will be confirming Xi’s belief that time is on China’s side.
insights.locator: But China does not need to win

insights.claim: Trump's policies exposed how vulnerable the U.S. economy is to Chinese actions, narrowing policy options for future administrations.
insights.speaker: Nicholas Bequelin, Yaqiu Wang
insights.so_what: Revealed U.S. vulnerabilities constrain future hawkish moves, favoring managed coexistence over decoupling shocks.
insights.locator: Taken together, it is striking
